# Synthetic test G-code

These files are generated by `tools/generate_samples.py`. They are released under the repo's MIT licence, so they're safe to share.

They're a 20 × 20 mm, 2 mm tall box with two walls and zigzag infill, 10 layers at 0.2 mm. Each file copies one slicer's conventions:

| File | Imitates | What it tests |
|---|---|---|
| `prusa_cube.gcode` | PrusaSlicer | `;LAYER_CHANGE`/`;Z:` markers, `;TYPE:` labels, `M82` absolute E, `estimated printing time` footer |
| `bambu_cube.gcode` | Bambu Studio | `;TYPE:Outer wall`-style labels, `total filament length` footer |
| `cura_cube.gcode` | Cura | `;LAYER:n` markers, `G92 E0` each layer, `;TIME:` header, meters-based footer |
| `relative_e_cube.gcode` | Mixed | `M83` relative extrusion, `G91`/`G90` relative XY block |
| `edge_cases.gcode` | Deliberately awkward | CRLF line endings, `G2` arc, `G92` reset mid-file, z-hop, unknown `T`/`M` codes, inline comments |

`expected.json` lists the values a correct parser should produce for each file: layer count, Z range, bounding box, net filament length (mm), and print time (s).

- Filament is the net sum of all E movement, so retractions cancel out.
- Time includes Z moves, and ignores acceleration. Real slicer estimates include acceleration, so they will differ slightly.
- `edge_cases.gcode` has about 0.23 mm more filament than the others because of the arc.

To regenerate: `python tools/generate_samples.py`
